toolchain.includeSearch: default system include search plus the explicitly selected pinned-image builtin headers

oracleDriver.installTree: not retained; the original driver and frontend are mounted read-only; image phase helpers are selected by the declared environment

oracleFrontend.scope: read-only mount for every orchestration case

referenceInvocationPolicy.imageAuthentication: the exact pinned image config is verified before every container invocation
referenceInvocationPolicy.cases: only the exact versioned arguments and staged input bytes listed in cases are admitted
referenceInvocationPolicy.phaseTools: unknown or malformed planned commands are rejected; each parsed planned or verbose phase path must match a declared phaseTools path or its explicit invokedAs name
referenceInvocationPolicy.producedPrograms: only the named output of a successful reference case; executable, interpreter and library bytes are rechecked before exec in a read-only workspace with only the fixed environment and PATH
referenceInvocationPolicy.runtimeScope: ELF interpreter and transitive startup libraries from the pinned loader --list; the linker plugin is inspected separately; kernel vDSO is identified by name, not image-owned bytes
referenceInvocationPolicy.executionEvidence: GCC plans and verbose transcripts are reference observations, not independent exec receipts; candidate enforcement and authenticated Kotlin-owned consumption remain required

capture.independentRepetition: each case ran twice in fresh workspaces with byte-identical results
capture.runsPerRepetition: `gcc -###` for the planned phases, `gcc -v` for the phases actually started, then the plain command for exit status, streams and artifacts; linked programs are then run in the same sandbox

temporary-file-names.replacement: <tmp-N> plus the original suffix, N numbering distinct names in order of first appearance per stream
temporary-file-names.reason: the driver draws temporary file names from mkstemp, so they differ between otherwise identical runs
temporary-file-names.appliesTo: driver plans, verbose traces and execution streams; artifacts are never normalized
